title: Phishing via Signal and Telegram targets European journalists and politicians, Le Monde reports
date_note: Date of the UNN and Slovo i Delo articles relaying Le Monde's investigation; neither gives an earlier day for the report. The campaign is said to have run since at least mid-October.
place: France (Le Monde's reporting; targets across Europe)
geo_basis: country of the reporting outlet and one named target (French MP); targets are in several European countries
summary: Citing Le Monde, UNN, Slovo i Delo, AzerNews and Meduza report a phishing campaign via Signal and Telegram against European journalists and politicians, running since at least mid-October; links led to fake pages. Three Le Monde journalists received an invitation on 17 November. Meduza, citing Agentstvo, says Christo Grozev got a fake Google Meet link leading to a fake Telegram login page. Le Monde's sources link it to UNC5792.
plain: Fake messages from supposed acquaintances on Signal and Telegram are reportedly being used to steal logins from European journalists and politicians. The reports rely on Le Monde and its sources.
exec: Messaging-app phishing aimed at journalists and politicians is reported; the attribution comes from Le Monde's sources and has not been read at the original.
action: General advice: treat unexpected invitations to video calls or Telegram groups, even from known contacts, as suspect, and confirm them through another channel before clicking.
impact: Named targets in the reports include Christo Grozev, Bastian Obermayer, three Le Monde employees and French MP Eric Bothorel.

validation.note: UNN and Slovo i Delo both relay one Le Monde investigation, so this is a single source; Le Monde's original was not read (lemonde.fr could not be fetched on 23 Nov). Attribution to UNC5792 and an FSB unit is by Le Monde's sources and (per the articles) US authorities, not confirmed by a page read here. AzerNews also relays the same Le Monde investigation and says the FSB attribution rests on the findings and assessments cited by Le Monde, not an independently established conclusion; it cites no government statement. Meduza (23 Nov, read) relays Le Monde and Agentstvo; it adds that Grozev and Bastian Obermayer received the same Signal message linking to a fake Google Meet call and a fake Telegram login page. Agentstvo's page was read but shows no absolute date, so it is not listed as a source.
